section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section contains the header and date of the maamar, including the Torah portion and the eve of Chanukah 5726.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbos Parshas Vayeishev,
Erev Chanukah,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Chanukah candles differ from the Temple Menorah in number, location, and time, and questions why the mitzvah is specifically outdoors.
section.t: To understand the matter of Chanukah candles,
that although the Chanukah candles were instituted because of the miracle that occurred with the candles of the Temple,
and whatever the Sages instituted is in the manner of Torah law they instituted,
nevertheless, they differ in several matters.
In their number—
for in the Menorah in the Temple there were seven candles,
and the Chanukah candles are eight.
In their place of standing—
for the Menorah was inside
(within the Sanctuary)
and in the south
(right side),
and the Chanukah candles are commanded to be placed outside
and on the left.
And in the time of their lighting—
for the Temple candles were lit from the time of the afternoon offering,
a duration of time
(an hour and a quarter)
before sunset,
and the mitzvah of the Chanukah candle is from sunset.
And adds my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe,
(in the continuation of "Padeh BeShalom" 5704)
another precision in this: that the Chanukah candle is commanded to be placed outside,
for we do not find a mitzvah
(except for the Red Heifer)
that must be outside
(the public domain)
specifically.
And he explains in the continuation,
that the simple reason for this, that the Chanukah candle is outside, is for the sake of publicizing the miracle.
But at first glance this reason is insufficient,
for the miracle of Purim is also publicized through a festive meal, sending portions, and gifts to the poor,
and nevertheless, this is not done in the public domain.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that Chanukah candles illuminate the darkness of the public domain, representing a light above the chain of descent, hence eight candles.
section.t: B)
And the point of the explanation in this is
(as explained in the discourses),
that the matter of Chanukah candles is to illuminate the darkness.
For through the war of the Greeks to cause them to forget Your Torah and to make them transgress the statutes of Your will,
[and particularly after they entered the Sanctuary and defiled all the oils in the Sanctuary],
there was a strengthening of the darkness of the side of impurity,
and therefore,
when the kingdom of the Chashmonaim prevailed and they defeated the Greeks, they instituted the Chanukah candles,
in order to illuminate the darkness.
And this is why their lighting time is from sunset,
for their matter is to illuminate the darkness.
And their place of standing is outside
(the public domain)
and on the left,
in order to also illuminate the darkness of the public domain,
the "mountains of separation,"
whose nourishment is from the left side.
And this is why the Chanukah candles are eight candles,
for that the Chanukah candles illuminate the darkness
(even the darkness of the public domain)
is because the light of the Chanukah candles is a light that is above the chain of descent,
and therefore they are eight candles,
for the number eight indicates a level that is above the chain of descent.
And likewise regarding the festival of Chanukah,
that the festival of Chanukah is eight days
(the days of Chanukah are eight),
it is,
because the revelation that shines during the days of Chanukah is a revelation that is above the chain of descent.
